arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import parse

# Test R1: 'l' type for letters only  
p = parse.Parser('{name:l}')
r = p.parse('hello')
print('R1 - letters match:', r.named['name'])

# Should NOT match digits
r2 = p.parse('123')
print('R1 - digits should not match:', r2)

# Test R2: __contains__ on Result
p3 = parse.Parser('{name} {age:d}')
r3 = p3.parse('John 25')
print('R2 - name in result:', 'John' in r3)
print('R2 - age in result:', 25 in r3)
print('R2 - key in result:', 'name' in r3)

# Test R3: Brace validation with actual unmatched braces
try:
    parse.Parser('{name')
    print('ERROR: Should have raised error for unmatched opening brace')
except ValueError as e:
    print('R3 - correct error for unmatched opening brace:', str(e))

try:
    parse.Parser('extra }name}')
    print('ERROR: Should have raised error for unmatched closing brace')
except ValueError as e:
    print('R3 - correct error for unmatched closing brace:', str(e))

# Escaped braces should be OK
p4 = parse.Parser('{{escaped}} {name}')
r4 = p4.parse('escaped hello')
print('Escaped braces work:', repr(r4.fixed), repr(r4.named))

# Test Match class __contains__
p5 = parse.Parser('{name:l}')
m = p5.search('hello world')
print('Match type:', type(m).__name__)
if hasattr(m, 'evaluate_result'):
    result = m.evaluate_result()
    print('Match.__contains__ works:', 'hello' in m)
" 2>&1 | grep -v SyntaxWarning | grep -v "^$"
